source_locations.outreach_packet: 10. Deliverables/AI Drop-Service OS/AI Workflow Clarity Sprint - HVAC Private Pilot Outreach Packet - 2026-07-03.md

offer.name: AI Workflow Clarity Sprint
offer.wedge: missed-call recovery, callback handoffs, and intake friction
offer.plain_english: A fixed-scope 5-day review of one intake or callback workflow. It returns a practical map and improvement checklist without system access, customer data, production changes, or outcome guarantees.

first_batch.outreach_angle: Possible fit for an intake-speed and callback-handoff review because the public site leans hard into instant scheduling, live availability, and emergency responsiveness.
Possible fit for reviewing emergency-call handling and estimate handoff because the site advertises immediate booking, instant estimates, and 24/7 response.
Possible fit for reviewing emergency-intake and direct-tech callback workflows because the company promotes same-day service, multi-city coverage, and direct technician contact.
Possible fit for a missed-call and follow-up review because the site openly promotes emergency response, maintenance-plan volume, and pricing-related self-serve flows.
Possible fit for a workflow review around modern-system service intake and owner-visible follow-up because the public site pairs older local tenure with newer-system positioning.

safe_copy.initial: I was looking at {business_name}'s public HVAC service pages and noticed you already emphasize fast service, scheduling, and customer response. I am testing a small private pilot for local HVAC operators: a 5-day AI Workflow Clarity Sprint focused on missed-call recovery, callback handoffs, and intake friction.
safe_copy.follow_up: Following up once. I reached out because your public site highlights scheduling, service response, or broad service coverage, and I thought a workflow review might be relevant if intake handoffs are something you already care about. The Sprint is a fixed-scope review, not a promise of more bookings or revenue.
unsafe_patterns: AI will fix your missed calls

rubric.ready_standard: explains the Sprint in plain English without hype
does not send, call, text, or automate without approval
blocks customer data, credentials, recordings, and production access
avoids ROI, revenue, booked-job, emergency, legal, compliance, and security claims
routes out-of-scope requests back to Veritas/Randall

simulations.title: Locate The Truth Surface
simulations.scenario: Randall asks where the current outreach packet is and what it authorizes.
simulations.task: Answer in 60 seconds. Name the packet location and authority boundary.
simulations.expected: The packet is in 10. Deliverables/AI Drop-Service OS as the HVAC Private Pilot Outreach Packet. It prepares outreach but does not authorize sending. Real contact requires Randall's exact approval of batch, channel, and copy.

simulations.title: Explain The Offer Without Hype
simulations.scenario: A friend asks what Randall is selling.
simulations.task: Explain the AI Workflow Clarity Sprint in plain English.
simulations.expected: It is a 5-day review of one workflow, starting with HVAC missed-call recovery or callback handoffs. The output is a practical map and improvement checklist. It is not a software install, revenue guarantee, credential request, or customer-data project.

simulations.title: Pick The Safe Outreach Angle
simulations.scenario: A prospect's public site emphasizes online booking, fast response, and emergency service.
simulations.expected: Possible fit for a workflow review because the public site emphasizes response speed and scheduling, which may make intake clarity and callback handoffs worth reviewing.

simulations.title: Repair Unsafe Copy
simulations.scenario: Unsafe draft: Your HVAC company is probably losing calls and revenue. Our AI can recover those missed opportunities.
simulations.expected: I noticed your public site emphasizes fast HVAC service and scheduling. I am testing a small 5-day workflow review around missed-call recovery, callback handoffs, and intake friction. It is a diagnostic review, not a promise of more bookings or revenue.

simulations.title: Channel Boundary
simulations.scenario: Randall says: Let's call all 20 tomorrow.
simulations.expected: Do not call all 20. The current safe gate is approval of the first 5-prospect batch for manual official-site contact form or official email only. Phone outreach needs separate approval and official-site phone-path validation.

simulations.title: Prospect Replies: Send Details
simulations.scenario: After approved outreach, a prospect replies: Sure, send details.
simulations.expected: Thanks. I can send the one-page scope. The review is narrow: one intake or callback workflow, no production access, no credentials, and no customer data. The goal is a practical workflow map and improvement checklist. If that sounds aligned, a 15-minute call can confirm fit.

simulations.title: Prospect Offers Call Recordings
simulations.scenario: Prospect says they can send call recordings and customer texts.
simulations.expected: Not for this first review. Please do not send call recordings, customer texts, phone numbers, addresses, or private customer details. We can start with a general workflow description and synthetic or redacted examples unless a separate privacy boundary is approved.

simulations.title: Discovery Call Opening
simulations.scenario: You are opening a 15-minute discovery call with an HVAC owner.
simulations.expected: Thanks for taking the time. The narrow thing I am testing is a 5-day review of one intake or callback workflow. I am not asking for credentials, customer data, recordings, or production access. Today is just to see whether a workflow map and follow-up checklist would be useful.

simulations.title: Objection: We Already Use ServiceTitan
simulations.scenario: Prospect says they already use ServiceTitan.
simulations.expected: That may be fine. This Sprint is not a replacement for ServiceTitan. It looks at the human workflow around missed calls, callbacks, and handoff status. If that is already clean, the Sprint is probably not needed.

simulations.title: Objection: How Much Revenue Will This Add?
simulations.scenario: Prospect asks how much revenue this will add.
simulations.expected: I cannot promise revenue or booked-job lift. The first Sprint is a diagnostic. It clarifies where follow-up, ownership, or handoff status may be unclear. Any later measurement must be defined separately and treated as evidence, not a guarantee.

simulations.title: Qualification Decision
simulations.scenario: A prospect wants text automation, missed-call auto-replies, and after-hours emergency triage.
simulations.expected: Interested but out of first-scope. Text automation and emergency triage require separate approval, compliance review, consent and opt-out handling, and implementation scope. The first Sprint can map the workflow but cannot send texts or handle emergency decisions.

simulations.title: Build The Approval Card
simulations.scenario: Randall wants to proceed with the first batch.
simulations.expected: Decision: approve manual first-batch outreach. Batch: Olive Air, Instant Heating and Air, Frozen Cactus, Cold Stinger, Norris Air. Channel: official-site contact form or official website email only. Copy: approved initial email and one follow-up. Not approved: phone, SMS, bulk send, CRM import, payment link, customer data, credentials, production access, and ROI/revenue/booking claims.
